chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Abdullah ibn Bahr from Hariz from Zurarah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Zurarah, what do you say about a man who leaves behind his parents and his brothers from his mother?' I said: 'One-sixth for the mother, and whatever remains is for the father.'
He said: 'From where?' I said: 'I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying in His Book: "If he has brothers, then for his mother is one-sixth."'
He said to me: 'Woe to you, O Zurarah! Those brothers are from the father. So if the brothers are from the mother, they do not prevent the mother from receiving one-third.'
ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers reduce the mother's inheritance share to one-sixth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the critical Shia jurisprudential distinction between full/paternal siblings and maternal siblings in inheritance law. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects Zurarah by clarifying that the Quranic restriction of the mother's share to one-sixth applies only when there are full or paternal siblings, whereas maternal siblings do not reduce her share from one-third, demonstrating the precision required in applying general Quranic verses to specific familial relationships.
